prompt: Our CDN/edge cache node sits in front of a bandwidth-shielded origin store. Popular objects (say, a viral thumbnail) are cached at the edge with a fixed TTL: on a cache HIT we return the stored body, and on a MISS we fetch the full object from origin, write it back with a fresh TTL, and return it. One hot key alone drives thousands of requests per second, and in production the origin shows sharp, periodic load spikes that line up exactly with the TTL interval rather than steady load. Here's the current edge read-path implementation — walk me through why the origin gets hammered every time this key expires, and optimize the code so that stops happening, without simply making the TTL longer.
